sections.h2: Start with town and county paperwork
sections.html:
Look at what the town holds about your house before you list it. Its website offers pages on Permits and Inspections, Code Compliance, Property Registration and flooding. If work was left half done or a code case is still open, settle it now rather than letting a title search turn it up.

Hurricane Preparedness pages and a Flood Awareness link are on the same site. Storm and insurance questions come up often with South Dade buyers, and you can point them to these pages.

The newest estimate is 44,750 residents, a dip of 1.5 percent from the 45,426 recorded in April 2020. Owners live in 69.7 percent of the homes spread over 9.89 square miles.

sections.h2: Commute and what to say in your listing
sections.html: The trip to work takes 38.2 minutes on average here, far above the national 26.4. Easy road access therefore counts for something. Mention a short drive to a main road if your street has one, and name a bus or highway route only after you have checked it yourself. A listing that reads as accurate and specific earns more trust than one that sounds like an advertisement, and trust shortens negotiations a great deal.

sections.h2: The Miami-Dade appraiser's South Dade branch
sections.html:
A regional branch of the county appraiser operates inside Cutler Bay, on the second floor of the South Dade Government Center at 10710 SW 211 Street. Walk-in hours run weekdays, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Call 305-232-3810 or book online.

Billing and collection belong to the county tax collector, and this office does not set rates. Appeals go to the Value Adjustment Board, which can still change a value. The Online Exemptions tool accepts widow and veteran disability filings.

Deeds in this county carry a tax of 60 cents on every $100. A surtax of 45 cents per $100 is layered on top, but a transfer that conveys just a single-family house skips it. The base rate is set out in s. 201.02, and each person who signs is liable for payment.

  • The clerk collects the tax at recording.
  • Page one costs $5.00 and each later page $4.00.
  • Two witnesses must watch you sign, and they can do so by audio-video link.

You can also register with the county Clerk of Court and Comptroller for a free alert, delivered within 24 hours, any time a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name.

sections.h2: Homestead and the Save Our Homes cap
sections.html:
Your taxable value stays below market while you own the house, thanks to a cap equal to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. The state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. The cap does not survive a sale.

  • The homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of value, and school taxes get the first $25,000 of it.
  • On the next January 1, the new owner is assessed at just value.
  • For a move inside Florida, portability can carry as much as $500,000 of savings to the next house if you file by March 1.

A buyer who assumes your bill carries over should first try the appraiser's estimator.

sections.h2: If a tenant, an heir or a lender is involved
sections.html:
The clock runs differently for each. Missed rent earns a tenant 3 days, a month-to-month tenancy needs 30 days' notice to end, and once a court has ruled the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice.

  • Heirs generally need a personal representative before anything can be signed. Estates of $150,000 or less may take the short route.
  • If a lender sues, the court sale is held 20 to 35 days after judgment.
  • Someone holding a tax certificate must wait two years from April 1 of the issue year to apply for a deed.

Ask a Florida attorney or the clerk which of these applies to you.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and the closing split
sections.html:
The state calendar is simple. Values are set January 1, exemption filing ends March 1, notices come in August, bills in November, and unpaid tax is delinquent from April 1. A petition on value must reach the clerk within 25 days of the notice.

A spring or summer closing leaves a whole November bill unpaid, and you and the buyer share it. Look for the proration on the settlement statement, then check it against the collector's record for your folio.

sections.h2: Senior and veteran benefits that end at sale
sections.html:
Each of these Florida benefits is attached to the house, so find out from the appraiser how it applies before you list.

  • Owners 65 and older may qualify for an additional exemption, up to $50,000, if the local ordinance permits it and household income is within the limit.
  • A veteran past 65 with a permanent disability from service can get a discount matching the VA percentage.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember rated at 10 percent or more receives $5,000 off.
  • Deferral through Form DR-570 must be filed by March 31.

With 16.9 percent of residents at 65 or older, many local owners may be affected.

Rent of $1,978 makes holding the house as a rental tempting. Landlords live with the notice rules above, and the tax bill can climb once homestead protection is gone. Weigh the repair calls and empty months before you commit.

If you do sell, note that 63.5 percent of residents aged five and up use another language at home and 64.0 percent are Hispanic or Latino. Listing text in two languages, plus a translated outline of your terms, will reach more buyers.

Put the deed, newest tax bill, lender payoff figure and permit records in a single folder. Review the town's Property Registration page too. Take dated photos of the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanical systems, so your description of the house is backed by pictures. Once offers come in, find out who covers title and recording and how each buyer will pay. Read the proration lines carefully on the settlement statement before you sign.

It also pays to think about moving day. Decide when the house will be empty, who will hold the keys, and which utilities need to be switched off or transferred. Leave garage openers, manuals and warranty papers for the new owner, and keep your own copies of the closing documents. Ask the title company when funds will reach you so you can plan the next purchase or rental around that date. If a buyer asks to move in early or to stay behind after closing, put the terms in writing with exact dates before you agree

faqs.q: What does a Cutler Bay home typically cost?
faqs.a: The typical owned home is valued at $472,700 for 2020-2024.
Slightly the other way. The 2025 estimate of 44,750 is 1.5 percent under the 2020 base.

faqs.q: Does the surtax apply to my Cutler Bay deed?
faqs.a: No, if the document moves only a single-family dwelling. The 60 cents per $100 base tax still applies.

faqs.q: Where can I get help with an exemption?
faqs.a: Visit the county appraiser's Cutler Bay branch at the South Dade Government Center, or use its online exemption filing.
The Miami-Dade tax collector, each November, with 4 percent off for paying that month.
